The Railway Claims Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1989 – Implementation of 
 123rd Report of the Committee. 
  
The Railway Claims Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1989 framed under the Railways 
Claims Tribunal Act, 1989 were examined by the Committee and the matter was reported 
to the House on the 21 st December, 1998 in its 123 rd Report wherein the Committee had 
recommended as under : - 
            “The Committee considered the subject at its meeting held on September 8, 1998 
and noted the comments of the Ministry of Railways in respect of Rules 17, 27 (2) and (3), 
30 and 33.   As regards the rules 11(3), 22, 32(2) and 3 1(1), the Committee noted with 
satisfaction that the Ministry had accepted its suggestion.  The Committee expressed the 
desire that the Ministry of Railways should carry out necessary amendment to the 
relevant rules, where Committees’ suggestion have been accepted expeditiously.” (para 
4.4) 
  
2.         Relevant extracts from the 123 rd Report were forwarded to the Ministry of 
Railways (Railway Board) on the 22 nd April, 1999 for implementation of its 
recommendations. 
  
3. The Ministry of Railways vide their communication dated the 21 st November, 2000 
informed as under: 
“The recommendation of the Committee to change Rules 11(3), 22, 31(1) and 32(2) have 
been examined in consultation with the Legislative Department of the Ministry of Law 
and Justice. 
            Legislative Department opined that the proposed amendments in Rule 11(3) & 22 
relating to removal of defects in the application before Registrar and the summoning of 
witnesses by the Tribunal recording the reasons in writing, are free from any legal 
difficulties.  The same can be carried out. 
  
The amendment proposed in Rule 31(1) relates to passing of an order either at once or as 
soon as thereafter but not later than 30 days from the date of conclusion of evidence and 
arguments.  The amendment prescribing the time limit of 30 days imposes a bar on the 
exercise of jurisdiction, and therefore would be outside the scope of the Act. 
            Regarding Rule 32(2) it has been opined that when Review is not provided by the 
substantive Act, it cannot be provided by means of Rule.  The provision of appeal, review 
or revision are made by the substantive Act and it relates to the jurisdiction and powers 
of a Tribunal.   Rules cannot provide appeal or review if it is not provided by the 
substantive Act. 
             
Rule 11(3) & Rule 22  are being amended as suggested by the Committee.   In so far as 
Rules 31(1) & 32(2)  are concerned, the Committee may like to reconsider the proposed 
amendments in view of the aforesaid legal implications and advise.”             
4.         The Committee considered the matter at its meeting held on the 16 th September, 
2004.  The Committee noted that the Ministry of Railways have implemented all the 
recommendations of the Committee as contained in its 123 rd Report on the Railway 
Claims ( Procedure) Rules, 1989 except those relating to rules 31(1) and 32(2).   The 
Committee was not convinced with the explanation furnished by the Ministry for their 
inability to implement its recommendations and decided to pursue the matter with the 
Ministry. 

5.         Accordingly, vide this Secretariat O.M. dated the 8 th October, 2004, the Ministry 
of Railways were requested to reconsider their stand on the Committee’s 
recommendations on these two rules in the light of the provisions of the Railway Claims 
Tribunal Act. 
6.         The Ministry of Railways vide their communication dated the 24 th March, 2005 
informed that the amendments to Rules 31(1) and 32(2) had since been notified vide 
  
G.S.R 173 (E) dated the 16 th March, 2005 publishing the Railway Claims T ribunal 
(Procedure) Amendment Rules, 2005. 
  
7.         The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Railways have 
amended the rules as per its suggestions as follows: - 
(i) Rule 11(3)    by providing that if on scrutiny an application, is fo und defective and 
defect noticed is formal in nature, the Registrar may allow the applicant to rectify the 
same in his presence, and if the defect is not formal in nature, the Registrar may allow 
the applicant to rectify defect in a week’s time, which may be extended in appropriate 
cases on the written request of the applicant. 
 
(ii) Rule 22(1)   by providing that if an application is presented by any party to the 
proceedings for summoning of witness, the Tribunal shall issue summons for the 
appearance of such witness by recording the reasons for doing so, unless it considers that 
the appearance of the witness is not necessary for the just decision of the case. 
 
(iii) Rule 31(1)   by substituting that the Tribunal, after hearing the applicant and 
respondent, shall pass an order either at once, or as soon as thereafter, as may be 
practicable but not later than twenty -one days from the date of conclusion of the 
arguments; and where is it unable to do so, it shall record its reasons for such inability; 
and  
 
(iv) Rule 32(2)   by substituting that where it appears to the Tribunal that there is no 
sufficient ground for a review, it shall reject the application and record its reasons for so 
doing.

IV 
  
The Railways (Opening for Public Carriage of  Passengers)    Rules, 2000-
Implementation 
 of 149th Report of the Committee. 
  
The Railways (Opening for Public Carriage of Passengers) Rules, 2000 were included in 
the 149th Report of the Committee presented to the House on the 19 th August, 2003. The 
Committee in the 149th Report had recommended as under: 
  
"The Committee considered the comments of the Ministry on the questionnaire at its 
meetings held on the 7 th May, 2003. The  Committee notes with satisfaction that the 
Ministry of Railways have accepted the Committee's suggestions on (i) Rule 19 
Explanation to modify the provision so as to specify the documents or types of documents 
required to be forwarded to the Commissioner for initiation of electric traction on a line; 
and (ii) Rule 24(5) to substitute the words "earliest opportunity" with suitable words so 
as to specify that the action is taken within a time frame between period of initiation of 
diversion and use of such temporary diversion to ensure prompt action on the part of the 

Commissioner. The Committee however, recommends that Rule 24(4) may be amended 
by substituting the words "responsible officer" with the words "Railway servant in 
charge of the work" in view of th eir comments. The Committee hopes that the Ministry 
would carry out these amendments expeditiously under intimation to it". 
  
2.         Relevant extracts from the 149 th Report were forwarded to the Ministry of 
Railways for necessary action on the 22 nd August, 2003. The Ministry vide their 
communication dated the 24 th May, 2004 furnished Action Taken Note on Rules 24 (4) 
and 24(5). The Committee considered the matter at its meeting held on the 7 th January, 
2005. The points referred to the Ministry, their co mments received thereon and the 
observations of the Committee are reproduced below:- 
  
I           POINT REFERRED 
  
Rule 24 (4) regarding substitution of the words "responsible officer" with the words 
"Railway servant in charge of the work." 
  
            Ministry's reply 
  
            The suggestion made by the Committee in their last para regarding Rule 24 (4) 
has been accepted by the Ministry of Railways and the same has been sent along with 
other necessary amendments to the said rules to Ministry of Law , Justice and Company 
Affairs (Legal Section) for their legal vetting so that the said rules can be published in the 
gazette. The proposed amendments are still under correspondence with the legal Ministry 
and the issue is likely to be sorted out soon. 
  
Committee’s observations (7.1.2005) 
  
            The Committee noted that the Ministry are taking necessary action with regard to 
making changes in rule 24 (4) in pursuance to its recommendations. 
  
II          POINT REFERRED 
  
Rule 24 (5) regarding substitution of the words 'earliest opportunity' with suitable 
words so as to specify that action is taken within a time frame between period of initiation 
of diversion and use of such temporary diversion to ensure prompt action on the part of 
the Commissioner. 
  
            Ministry's reply 
  
            So far as the recommendation of the Committee regarding Rule 24 (5) is 
concerned, Ministry has decided not to make any change. 
  
            Committee’s observations (7.1.2005) 
  
            The Committee was not satisfied with the comments of the Ministry on rule 24 
(5).  It took exception to the Ministry’s statement that they had “decided not to make any 
change” in rule 24 (5) and desired that the Ministry may be asked to furnish a detailed 
justification why the Committee’s recommendations in relation to rule 24 (5) are not 
acceptable to them.    
  

3.         Accordingly, a reference was sent to the Ministry on the 5 th May, 2005.   The 
Ministry of Railways furnished Action Taken Note on the 3 rd May, 2005.  The Ministry 
have amended and notified Rule 24 (4) as per the Committee’s suggestion by substituting 
the words “responsible officer” with the words “railway servant in-change of work”.  
  
            Regarding Rule 24(5), the Ministry have furnished a detailed note justifying  their 
non-acceptance of the Committee’s suggestion on the said rule which is reproduced 
below: 
  
            “The Committee’s recommendation as contained in its 149th Report in relation to 
Rule 24 (5) could not be agreed to particularly in view that the day safety of the running 
trains is the responsibility of the Ministry of Railways and not that of the 
Commissioner.  As can be seen from the Section 6 of the Railways Act, 1989, the duties of 
the Commissioner are as given below:- 
  
Inspect any railway with a view to determine whether it is fit to be opened for the public 
carriage of passengers and report thereon to the Central Government as required by or 
under this Act. 
  
Make such periodical or other inspections of any railw ay or of any rolling stock used 
thereon as the Central Government may direct. 
  
Make an inquiry under this Act into the cause of any accident on a railway.  
  
Discharge such other duties as are conferred on him by or under this Act.   
  
Therefore, keeping the above in view, the provision under Rule 24 (5) for inspection of 
the temporary diversion continuing for more than 3 days by the Commissioner has been 
kept as discretionary rather than making it mandatory.  Therefore, it has been stipulated 
in Rule 24(5) that Commissioner may inspect it at the “earliest opportunity” rather than 
fixing any definite time limit.  
  
It is hoped that the Committee would appreciate the view of the Railway Ministry”. 
  
In accordance to their explanation as given above, the Mini stry have amended and 
notified Rule 24(5) by substituting sub rule (5) of rule 24 so as to provide that “where the 
use of temporary diversion as likely to be extended to more than 3 days, the 
Commissioner shall, if he considers it necessary, take the earliest possible opportunity of 
inspecting it”. 
  
4.         The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Railways have since 
published the Railways (Opening for Public Carriage of Passengers) (Amendment) Rules, 
2005 vide notification No. G.S.R. 44(E) dated the 27 th January, 2005 (i) modifying the 
provisions of Rule 19  Explanation so as to provide that when sanction is required for the 
initiation of electric traction on a line already opened for passenger traffic, the documents 
specified in terms (j), (k), (l), (m) and (n) of sub rule (1), item (d) of sub rule (2) and item 
(a) (vii) of sub rule 5 shall be forwarded to the Commissioner; and (ii) in case of   rule 
24(4)  by substituting the words ‘responsible officer’ with the words ‘servant-in-charge’. 
Regarding Rule 24(5), the Committee accepts the explanation furnished by the Ministry 
of Railways for non -revision of the provisions of Rule 24(5) as suggested by it.   The 
Committee, however,  notes that as a follow up to their explanation, the Ministry have 
since amended Rule 24 (5) by providing that “where the use of temporary diversion is 

likely to be extended to more than 3 days the Commissioner shall, if he considers it 
necessary, take the earliest possible opportunity of inspecting it.”

V 
  
The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001. 
  
            The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules , 2001 framed 
under the Prevention of Cruelty to animals Act, 1960 were examined and a questionnaire 
on the subject was forwarded to the Ministry of environment & Forests for their 
comments/clarifications on the 25 th November, 2003.   The Ministry furnished  their 
comments/clarifications on the 21st September, 2004.  The points referred to the Ministry 
and the comments/clarifications received thereon are reproduced below:- 
  
1          Point referred 
  
            The legislation under which these rules have been framed is of 1960.   In what 
manner the aspects covered by these rules were being regulated prior to framing of these 
rules? 
  
            Ministry comments 
  
            Prior to this legislation, the State governments/Local bodies formulated their own 
Rules and Regulations for functioning of the slaughter houses. 
  
II          Point referred 
            Rule 2 (c) Definition 
  
            “Slaughter house” means a slaughter house wherein 10   animals are slaughtered 
per day and is duly licensed or recognized under a Central, State or Provincial Act or any 
rules or regulations made thereunder”. 
  
            Are these rules applicable to such slaughter houses where less than 10 animals are 
slaughtered per day; why these have been excluded from the defini tion of “Slaughter 
House”? 
  
            Ministry’s comments 
  
            It may not be possible to depute so many veterinary officers to conduct the proper 
ant and post -mortem examination as the number of such places where animals are 
slaughtered in twos, threes, fours or even little more may be very high and at scattered 
places.  In addition to economic considerations, proper handling and disposal of slaughter 
wastes will be a problem.  Therefore, a minimum criterion of 10 animals to be slaughtered 
has been fixed to implement these Rules effectively and check the clandestine slaughter. 
  
III.       Point referred 
            Rule 4(2) Reception area or resting grounds 
  
            “The veterinary doctor shall examine thoroughly not more than 12 animals in an 
hour and not more than 96 animals in a day”. 
  

            Is it possible to examine 96 animals in a day which normally has eight working 
hours including lunch break? 
  
            Ministry’s comments 
  
            Depending on the species, time required for the examination varies.  The number 
specified is the maximum limit.   It is not mandatory for the veterinarian that he must 
examine 96 animals in a day. 
  
IV.       Point referred 
            Rule 4(3) Reception area or resting grounds. 
  
            “The veterinary doctor after examining the animal shall issue a fitness certificate 
in the form specified by the Central Government for this purpose”. 
  
            Whether Government h ave any objection in incorporating the format of fitness 
certificate in the rules itself? 
  
            Ministry’s comments 
  
            The format has to be in conformity with international/national requirements and 
therefore, this shall need modificatio n/amendments from time to time.   Hence not 
incorporated in the Rules itself. 
  
V.        Point referred 
            Rule 6(6) Slaughter  
  
            “A curbed -in bleeding area of adequate size as specified by the Central 
Government shall be provided in a  slaughter house and it shall be so located that the 
blood could not be splashed on other animals being slaughtered or on the carcass being 
skinned”. 
  
            What are the reasons that the Central Government have been authorized to 
specify the curbed -in bleeding area?   Does this size vary with the size of the Slaughter 
House and if so, can this function not be delegated to the State Governments or other 
local authority? 
  
            Ministry’s comments 
  
            The size of the slaughter house and species of the animals to be slaughtered shall 
govern the size of curbed -in bleeding area.   The implementing agencies are State 
Governments/Local bodies.   In order to maintain uniformity throughout the country, 
power has been vested with the Central Government.   
  
VI.       Point referred 
            Rule 9(1) Inspection of slaughter house  
  
            “The Animal Welfare Board of India or any person or Animal Welfare 
Organization authorized by it may inspect any slaughter house without notice to its owner 
or the person in charge of it at any time during the working hours to ensure that the 
provisions of these rules are being complied with”.  
  

What is the frequency of such inspections? Should the rules not prescribe a mini mum 
frequency of such inspections in every slaughter house so that the inspections are uniform 
and regular? 
The words ‘any person’ appear to be vague.  Whether Government have any objection in 
specifying the minimum level/status of such officer? 
  
Ministry’s comments 
  
The Government of India is agreeable to prescribe a minimum frequency of such 
inspections after working it out with the animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI), who are 
responsible for such inspections. 
  
The Government of India has no objection in specifying the minimum level/status of the 
inspecting officers in consultation with AWBI. 
  
2.         The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry have accepted its 
suggestions on point no. 6 on Rule 9(1) regarding inspection of slaughter h ouse to (i) 
prescribe a minimum frequency of inspection of slaughter houses so as to make such 
inspection uniform and regular; and (ii) to specify the minimum level/status of the 
inspecting officers.   On rest of the points, the committee accepts the Minist ry’s 
comments.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry of environment & forests would carry 
out the amendments to the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 
2001, expeditiously, under intimation to it.

inspecting officers.   On rest of the points, the committee accepts the Ministry’s 
comments.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry of environment & forests would carry 
out the amendments to the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rul es, 
2001, expeditiously, under intimation to it.

2.         During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has noted 
some cases where there has been a considerable time lag between the date of 
notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of delay in cases where notifications have not been laid as per 
the Committee’s guidelines and whether such notifications were accompanied by 
a statement indicating the reasons for the delay in laying. In some of the cases the 
delay has been quite abnormal. The observations/recommendations of the 
Committee in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments are as follows: 
(i)       Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers  
          (Department of Chemicals& Petrochemicals) 
  
            The Committee regrets to note that there is a delay of 6 months in the laying 
of the only notification laid by the Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers (Sl No. 5). 
The Ministry have appended a delay statement with the same. The Committee 
hopes that the Department of Chemical & Petrochemicals of the Ministry of 
Chemicals & Fertilizers would avoid such instances in future. 
  
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution  
            Department of Food & Public Distribution) 
  
The Committee regrets to note that there is a delay of 5 months in laying of one 
out of the five notifications laid by the Department of Food & Public Distribution 
of the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution (Sl No. 30). The 

Ministry have not appended a delay statement with the delayed notification.   The 
Committee hopes that the Ministry of Ministry of Consumer A ffairs, Food & 
Public Distribution would avoid such delays and would append a delay 
statement  in all such cases of delay in future. 
  
(iii)       Ministry of Finance  
(Department of Economic Affairs) 
  
The Committee notes that out of a total of   212 notifications laid by the 
Ministry of Finance (66 notifications by the Department of Economic Affairs and 
146 by the Department of Revenue) during the 207th Session, there is a delay in the 
laying of 2 notifications (Sl No. 39 & 44) by the Department of Economi c 
Affairs.  The Ministry have appended a delay statement with only one notification 
(Sl No. 44).  The reason for delay in laying the notification has been attributed to 
non receipt of the gazette copies from the Government of India Press by the Indian 
Bank.   The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Finance would avoid such 
instances in future.   The Committee also notes that the notification at Sl No. 97 
does not carry any distinctive number. In this context, the Committee would like 
to draw the Ministry’s attention towards its recommendation as contained in its 
152nd Report (relevant extracts reproduced later) whereby each notification must 
be allotted a distinctive number while notifying in the Gazette. The Committee 
hopes that the Ministry shall take care  of this aspect in future.    The Committee, 
however, appreciates that there is an overall decline in the instances of delay in 
the laying of notifications as compared to the position in earlier sessions and hopes 
that the Ministry of Finance would continue  with their efforts to avoid delay in 
laying of notifications and in case of any delay in their laying, shall keep the House 
informed of the reasons  for the same through delay statements. 
  
Ministry of Human Resource Development 
  
The Committee notes with  regret that the Ministry of Human Resource 
Development have delayed the laying of 3  notifications (Sl No. 269, 275 & 276) out 
of the 9 notifications laid by them.   While the Department of Elementary 
Education & Literacy have delayed the laying of one notification by 6 months, the 
Department of Secondary & Higher Education have delayed the laying of 2 of their 
notifications by 7 months and have also failed to append a delay statement.    The 
delay statement appended with the notification laid by the Departm ent of 
Elementary Education & Literacy (Sl No. 269) states the reason for delay as 
follows:- 
  
 “….The University notified the amendment on 1.8.2005 and got published the 
same in the Gazette of India Part III -Section IV on 20.8.2005.   Copies of the 
Gazette Notification were  sent by the University for laying on 10.10.2005.   These 
copies were received in the Ministry on 14.10.2005.  Copies duly authenticated by 
MOS (HRD) were received in the section on 16.12.2005.   This notification could 
not be laid in the Winter Session of Rajya Sabha due to the fact that the House 
was adjourned on 23.12.2005.” The Committee feel that the Ministry of Human 
Resource Development still had sufficient time to lay these notifications during the 
Winter Session 2005 if they had ac ted promptly.  The Committee recommends 
that Ministries should try to avail of the earliest opportunity to lay their papers 
before the Parliament rather than waiting for the later dates of the Session so as 
to avert eventualities like adjournment of the House pre mature.  The Committee 

also recommend the Ministry to invariably  append a delay statement  in all  cases 
of delay in future. 
  
(v)        Ministry of Labour & Employment 
  
The Committee is unhappy to note that out of the 4 notifications laid, the 
Ministry of Labour & Employment have delayed the laying of 2 of 
their  notifications (Sl No. 280 & 282).   Delay statement has been appended with 
both.  The delay statement for the laying of notification at Sl No. 280 states as 
under: 
  
“….at the time of la ying of the amendment incorporating a new Table ‘E’ and 
inclusion of para 39B after para  39A in the EPS, 1995 before Parliament, the Lok 
Sabha Secretariat pointed out that in all the amending rules, a footnote is required 
to be given at the end of the rul e containing therein the details of earlier 
amendments.  Thereafter, the Ministry inserted the requisite footnote by issuing a 
corrigendum to this effect and notifying the same in the Gazette on 16.8.2004, but 
a copy of the Gazette Notification was not rec eived in the Ministry.   Now the 
Notification has been obtained, which is why the delay.” 
  
The delay statement for the laying of notification at Sl No. 282 states, 
“…the copy of the Gazette Notification was received in the Ministry in February, 
2006, which is why the delay.” 
  
            The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Labour & Employment would 
take necessary corrective measures to avoid such instances in future. 
  
(vi)       Ministry of Power 
  
The Committee regrets to note that there is a delay of 6 months in laying of 
one out of the six notifications laid by the Ministry of Power (Sl No. 286). The 
Committee hopes that the Ministry of Power would avoid such instances in future. 
  
(vii)      Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions 
(Department of Personnel & Training) 
  
The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Personnel, Public 
Grievances & Pensions (Department of Personnel & Training) have laid 30 
notifications during the Session out of which 20 notifications (Sl No. 290-309) have 
been delayed.  While some notifications have been delayed by 6 -7 months, in 14 
cases there has been a delay of 1 year and 3 months. The Ministry have appended 
a delay statement with all the 20 delayed   notifications.  In their delay statement 
appended to the notifications, the Ministry have submitted as follows:- 
  
“The notification, which was sent to Government of India Press for 
publication in Part II Section 3 (i) of the Gazette of India on 12.9.2005, was 
published in the Extraordinary Gazette on 17.9.2005.  Due to administrative 
exigencies and frequent transfers of the officer dealing with the subject, the matter 
got delayed because the new incumbent needed time to acquaint himself with the 
procedure of publication, follow up with the Government of India Press for G.S.R. 
copies and laying down in both Houses of Parliament.   The delay in laying the 

notification in time is highly regretted.   This may be laid in both Houses of 
Parliament during the current session.” 
  
The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Personnel, Public 
Grievances & Pensions (Department of Personnel & Training) could not avail of 
the opportunity to lay the subordinate legislation not only during the Budget 
Session-2005 but also during the Monsoon and Winter Sessions of 2005 thereby 
delaying the laying of the notifications by one year.  Even in cases where there has 
been a delay of 6 -7 months, the Ministry could have laid the notifications during 
the Winter Session-2005.  The Committee is not satisfied with the reasons given by 
the Ministry for the delay and expects them to be prompt and vigilant in the laying 
of subordinate legislation within the stipulated period as recommended in its 131st 
Report (relevant extracts reproduced in para 3 of the report).   The Committee 
hopes that the Ministry will evolve some systematic procedure to avoid such 
instances in future. 
  
  
(viii)       Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport & Highways  
(Department of Road Transport & Highways) 
  
The Committee regrets to note that out of a total of 204 Notifications laid 
by the Department of Road Transport & Highways of the Ministry of Shipping, 
Road Transport & Highways, there has been a delay in the laying of 16 
notifications (Sl No. 336-341, 354-361, 374-375.  The delay ranges from 3½ months 
(Sl No. 355-361), 5 months (Sl No. 354 and 376), 8 months (Sl No. 341), 11 months 
(Sl No. 338-340), 1 year ( Sl No. 374 and 375), 2 years (Sl No. 337)  and 3 years (Sl 
No. 336).  A delay statement has been appended with all the notifications which  
states, “It took time to collect the papers and complete the procedural 
formalities.  As such the notifications could not be laid on the Table of both Houses 
of Parliament during the last session.”   The Committee expects the Ministry of 
Shipping, Road Transport & Highways to exercise caution in the matter of timely 
laying of subordinate legislation and ensure that the schedule prescribed by it in 
this behalf is followed meticulously.  The Committee recommends the Ministry to 
evolve some systematic procedure to avoid such instances in future. 
  
3.         The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take 
immediate steps to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation. The 
Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice o f all 
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, the defaulting 
ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 131 st,135th  and 152 nd 
Reports: 
            “Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if the House 
is not in Session, during the Session immediately following the date of publication 
of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, on the date 
of the publication of the Order, during its continuance and in case the time l ag 
between the date of publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less 
than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said 
Session. All the Ministries/Departments of Government of India should henceforth 
comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the Orders issued under 
various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.” 
(131st Report) 

            “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in 
case there is a dela y in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concerned 
Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay statement along with the 
notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliament of the causes of delay. The 
Committee desires all Ministries/Departments t o take a note of this, since the 
intension is that through the process of formulation of a delay statement the 
Ministry is able to introspect, identifying bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”. 
(135th Report) 
            “In the opinion of the Committe e, every notification should be assigned a 
distinctive number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, no 
notification should be published/laid which does not carry a notification number. 
The Committee expects all Ministries/Departments of Go vernment of India to 
exercise caution in this regard. In case where there are more than one notification 
under a single file, the Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file number 
on each notification should be suitably distinguished from one another. 
(152nd Report)

During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has noted 
some cases where there has been a considerable time lag between the date  
  

of notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed 
statement also indicates the period of delay in cases where notifications 
have not been laid as per the schedule prescribed by the Committee and 
whether such notifications were accompanied by a statement indicating 
the  
reasons for the delay in laying. In some of the cases the delay has been 
quite abnormal. The observations/recommendations of the Committee in 
respect of the specific Ministries/Departments are as follows:-    
             
(i) Ministry of  Environment & Forests 
  
            The Committee notes with regret that out of the four notifications 
laid by the Ministry of Environment & Forests during the 208th Session, 
there has been delay in case of  one (Sl. nos.17) and no delay statement has 
been appended with it.   The Committee would like the Ministry to take 
corrective measures so as to obviate such delay in future.  
  
(ii) Ministry of Finance  
     (Department of Economic Affairs) 
  
            The Committee notes that the Ministry of Finance (Department of 
Economic Affairs) have delayed the laying of four notifications (Sl.Nos. 
27,28,68&69) out of 57 notifications laid by them during the session. In all 
these four cases the Ministry have failed to append the delay 
statement.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Finance would 
continue with their efforts to avoid delay in laying of the notifications and 
in case of any delay actually taking place in laying, a delay statement 
would invariably be appended. 
(iii) Ministry of Finance  
      (Department of  Revenue) 
  
            The Committee regrets to note that there is a delay of 6 months to 
11 months in laying of two notifications out of the 105 notifications laid by 
the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) (Sl.Nos. 174 & 175) and 
the Ministry have not appended delay statement.  The Committee hopes 
that the Ministry would take necessary corrective steps in the matter. 
  
(iv)  Ministry of Home Affairs 
  
            The Committee is unhappy to note that out of the 5 notifications 
laid by the Ministry of Home Affairs there has been delay upto 10 months 
in the laying of three notifications ( Sl.Nos.189 to 191).  The Ministry have 
not appended delay statement with any of these delayed notifications 
either.  The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs 
should stick to the time schedule as recommended by it in its 131st Report 
in the matter of laying of Subordinate Legislation before Parliament and 
in case of any delay, the delay statement must also be appended so as to 
apprise the Parliament of the reasons that caused the delay. 

  
(v) Ministry of Labour & Employment  
  
            The  Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Labour & 
Employment have delayed the laying of one notification (Sl No. 201) out of 
2 laid by them and have not appended reason for delay with it.  The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry should make efforts to adhere 
to the time schedule prescribed for this purpose by the Committee and in 
case there is delay, a statement containing the reasons for such delay is 
also laid along with the notification. 
  
(vi) Ministry of Law & Justice  
     (Department of Legal Affairs) 
  
            The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of 
seven months on the part of the Ministry of Law and Justice in laying 
in  case of one of the two notifications laid by them (Sl. No.203). The 
Ministry have appended delay statement with the Notification and the 
reason given by the Ministry reads:-“ Writ Petitions were filed in various 
High Courts in January,2006 itself.  Accordingly, a Transfer Petition No. 
92/2006 was filed in the Hon’ble Supreme Court on 2nd February, 2006, 
Subsequently, some more Writ Petitions have been filed in different High 
Courts.  The Transfer Petition was mentioned in the Hon’ble Supreme 
Court on 18th July, 2006.  On a query. the Hon’ble Court was informed 
that the service has been done on the opposite parties, decision was 
expected from the Hon’ble Supreme Court earlier.  However, now it is 
likely to be decided shortly.  Due to this, the Rules could not be laid in the 
Budget Session of Parliament”.   
            The Committee notes the   reasons furnished by the Ministry for 
delay in laying in the delay statement The Committee hopes that the 
Ministry would take care to lay their rules/regulations on time in future. 
  
(vii) Ministry of Panchayati Raj and Youth Affairs & Sports 
  
            The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry have delayed 
the laying of all the four notifications (Sl.Nos. 205 to 208 )  by them. The 
Minsitry have appended delay statement with all the Notifications, the 
reasons given by the Ministry reads.- “The Andman & Nicobar 
Administration had notified (i) The Andaman & Nicobar Islands Gram 
Panchayats (Levy of Taxes and Fees) Rules, 2002, (ii) The Andman & 
Nicobar Islands Panchayats Samitis (Levy, Assessment, Collection and 
Appropriation of Taxes, Duties, Cess, Tolls and Fees) Rules, 2002, (iii) The 
Andaman & Nicobar Islands (Grant-in-aid to Panchayati Raj Institutions) 
(3rd Amendment) Rules, 2003, (iv) The Andaman & Nicobar Islands 
(Panchayats Administration) (Amendment) Rules, 2003 on 24 April, 2002 
and 21 August, 2003.      The Andaman & Nicobar Administration had 
forwarded copies of these rules to the Ministry of Home Affairs during 
February, 2003 as soon as copies of the notifications were available after 

publication.  The Ministry of Home Affairs forwarded these Rules to 
Ministry of Rural Development during May, 2003. Hindi version of the 
Notifications mentioned above could not be sent by the Andaman & 
Nicobar Administration at that time as the same were pending with the 
Central Translation Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs, New Delhi.  On 
receipt of Hindi versions of the Rules, 100 copies were forwarded to the 
Ministry of Home Affairs. The Ministry further have stated that in a 
request of this Ministry for sending 40 copies of each of the Rules, the 
Andaman & Nicobar Administration got them re-printed and forwarded 
copies to the Ministry of Rural development on 12/3/2006, as sufficient 
copies were not available at that time.  The delay in sending the copies 
from November 2005 to February, 2006 was due to the delay in getting the 
copies printed."   
 The Committee feels that the cause of the delay in laying of the Rules” is 
not justified as the same could have been pre-empted by sufficient copies 
printed in time. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of 
Panchayati Raj and Youth Affairs & Sports to take immediate steps to 
prevent such instances of delay in the laying of their subordinate 
legislation in future.  
  
(viii) Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions 
        (Department of Personnel & Training) 
  
The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Personnel, Public 
Grievances & Pensions (Department of Personnel & Training) have laid 
07 notifications during the Session out of which 03 notifications (Sl No. 
217-219) have been delayed.  Notifications have been delayed upto 11 
months. A delay statement has been appended with three notifications, 
reads:- “ Due to delay in receipt of printed copies of notification from 
Government of India Press and other administrative reason, the laying of 
the notification has been delayed”. The Committee is not convinced from 
the statement giving reason for delay laid by the Ministry. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry should make all efforts to avoid such delays 
in the laying of the notifications. 
  
(ix)       Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport & Highways  
      (Department of Road Transport & Highways) 
  
The Committee regrets to note that out of a total of 247 Notifications laid 
by the Department of Road Transport & Highways of the Ministry of 
Shipping, Road Transport & Highways, there has been  delay in the laying 
of only one notification (Sl No. 387) by 11 months. A delay statement has 
been appended with all the notifications, reads:- “It took time to collect 
the papers and complete the procedural formalities.  As such the 
notifications could not be laid on the Table of both Houses of Parliament 
during the last session.”   The Committee expects the Ministry of 
Shipping, Road Transport & Highways to exercise caution in the matter 

of timely laying of subordinate legislation and ensure that such delays do 
not recur.  
  
3.         The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to 
take immediate steps to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate 
legislation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all 
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, the 
defaulting ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 
131st,135th  and 152nd Reports: 
            “Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if 
the House is not in Session, during the Session immediately following the 
date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the 
House is in Session, on the date of the publication of the Order, during its 
continuance and in case the time lag between the date of publication and 
the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, before the 
expiry of the Session immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India should henceforth 
comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the Orders issued 
under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.” 
(131st Report) 
            “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential 
that in case there is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the 
concerned Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay 
statement along with the notifications being laid so as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intension is that 
through the process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is 
able to introspect, identify bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 
(135th Report) 
            “In the opinion of the Committee, every notification should be 
assigned a distinctive number in order to give it a separate identity and 
similarly, no notification should be published/laid which does not carry a 
notification number. The Committee expects all Ministries/Departments 
of Government of India to exercise caution in this regard. In case where 
there are more than one notification under a single file, the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file number on each 
notification should be suitably distinguished from one another. 
(152nd Report)

INTRODUCTION
 
 
1.         I, the Chairman of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, having been authorized by the Committee to present
the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this Hundred and Sixty-Seventh Report of the Committee.
 
1.2
        The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on the 6th March, 2007.

them along with the comments received from the Government.  The observations and recommendations of the Committee
are contained in the succeeding paragraphs of the Report.
 
 
NEW DELHI

Report
       I
                  The Counting of past service for pensionary benefits on mobility between Central Government and Central and
State Autonomous Bodies and vice-versa-Implementation of 117 th Report of the Committee on, Public Grievances and
Pensions, Public Grievances and Pensions Legislation, Rajya Sabha.
 
          "The Counting of past service for the purpose of pensionary benefits on mobility between the Central Government
and the Central and the State Autonomous bodies and vice-versa”  were examined and reported to the House by the
Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha on June 12, 1998 vide  its 117 th Report. Extracts from the Report
containing the Committee’s recommendations are enclosed (Annexure-I).  A copy of the report was forwarded to the
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions (Department of Pension and Pensioners Welfare) on June 16, 1998
with the request that the action taken  report of the Ministry on the recommendations made by the Committee may be
furnished within a period of three months.
 
2.         The Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions  vide their communication dated August 3, 1998 stated as
under: -
 

167th Report of Committee on Subordinate Legislation
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/167thReport.htm[25-10-2016 16:44:04]
“Recommendations of the Committee are being considered in this department but before taking a final decision on
the same the matter requires consultation with various departments including different division of Ministry of Finance.  It is
likely to take more than three months before final decision is arrived at. Further, all efforts will be made to settle the matter
within the stipulated time”.
 
3.         Later on, the Ministry vide their communication dated December 17, 1998 informed as under: -
 
“In order to decide the follow up action on the recommendations of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, the
department has constituted a Committee, which met on 25.8.98.  It has been felt that before taking a final decision in
the matter, it is necessary to work out the likely repercussions, particularly in view of the emerging changed
scenario, wherein the Banking and Insurance sectors are likely to open up to public equity participation, changing
drastically the institutional structures and affecting the conditions of service in these organizations.  It was also felt
that the arrangements of counting of past service has to be on reciprocal basis and, therefore, the institutions in the
Banking and Insurance sector need to be consulted before orders are issued in this regard.  This department is in the
process of consulting Banking/Insurance Division on these two issues.  Separately this department is also
ascertaining the views of the Attorney General in the matter. This Department is pursuing the matter vigorously.
Despite this, it is felt that final action is likely to take sometime in view of the intricacies involved in the matter, This
department, therefore, feels that it may not be possible to take final action in the matter within 6 months.  It is,
therefore, requested that Rajya Sabha Secretariat may please approach the Committee on Subordinate Legislation
for extension of time upto 31
st March 1999.  This department therefore, feels that it may be granted extension of time
up to 31st March 1999”.
 
4.         The Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions after being reminded, again sought further extension of
time upto 30th June, 1999.Thereafter, the Ministry vide their communication dated June 28, 1999 informed the Committee as
under:-
 
“That this department is in process of consulting banking/insurance division of the Ministry of Finance on the issue
of counting of service rendered in those Organisations together with the Central Government Service and vise-versa. In this
connection it may be mentioned here that a Committee of Officers consisting of Additional Secretary (Pension), Joint
Secretary (Pension), Joint Secretary (Insurance) and Deputy Secretary (Banking) of Ministry of Finance together with
Director (PW) of Department of Pension and P.W was constituted to consider the matter.  A final meeting of Committee was
held on 21.06.99 and matter now will be finalized on receipt of certain information, which is required from Insurance
Division of Ministry of Finance.  Thereafter, the proposal will be sent for approval of Ministry of Finance, department of
expenditure.  The above process is likely to take time of 6 months for which extension will be required from Committee on
Subordinate Legislation of Rajya Sabha. It is therefore, requested that Committee on Subordinate Legislation may be
approached for further extension of time upto 31
st December 1999. The process will require 6 months and therefore Ministry
have further approached for extension of time up to 31st December, 1999”.
 
5.         The Ministry was granted extension of time upto 31 st December,1999 but at the same time directed to furnish a bi-
monthly progress report in the matter regularly. Later, the Ministry vide their communication dated September 7, 1999
informed as under:-
    
 “On the receipt of recommendation from Committee on Subordinate Legislation of Rajya Sabha, this department
constituted a Committee of Officers consisting of Joint Secretary (Pers.) Ministry of Finance, Joint Secretary
(Insurance) Ministry of Finance, Deputy Secretary (Banking) Ministry of Finance, Addl. Secretary (Pension),
Director (PW), Department of Pension & PW to consider the matter relating to counting of service rendered in
Public Sector Banks including RBI/SBI and LIC/GIC etc. together with central Government Service, for pension

Cost Accounting Records (Electricity Industry) Rules, 2001.
 
            The Cost Accounting Records (Electricity Industry) Rules, 2001, framed under the Companies Act, 1956 were
examined and a questionnaire on the subject was forwarded to the Ministry of Company Affairs on the January 10, 2003 for
furnishing their comments. The Ministry vide
 their communication dated the 16th February, 2003 furnished their comments.
 
            The Committee considered the subject matter at its meeting held on the 15
th June, 2004. The Committee noted the
comments furnished by the Ministry on the various points raised in the questionnaire except on point no. 1 wherein it desired
that further clarifications be sought. Accordingly, further clarifications was sought on point no. 1 on the 31
st August, 2004,
and reply to the same was received on the 15 th September, 2004. The points raised, Ministry's comments and Committee's
recommendations are as follows:-
 
1.)        Point Raised:-
 
            The Cost Accounting Records (Electricity Industry) Rules, 2001 have been framed in exercise of powers conferred
by sections 642 (1) and 209 (1) (d) of the Companies Act, 1956. Clause (d) of sub section (1) of section 209 of the
Companies Act, which relates to keeping of proper books of accounts by a Company was added in the Act with effect from
the 15
th October, 1965. When did Government include electricity industry for the purposes of keeping proper books of
accounts in terms of section 209 of the Act?
 
            Ministry's Comments (16.02.03):-
 
            The Government, in terms of section 209 (1) (d) of the Act, notified the Cost Accounting Records (Electricity
Industry) Rules, 2001 on 21 st December, 2001 vide GSR 913 (E) requiring electricity industry to keep proper books of
account with effect from the financial year commencing on or after the publication of these rules.
 
            Further query by the Committee (31.08.04):-
 
            Specify the date with effect from which the Electricity Industry was included for the purpose of keeping proper books
of accounts in terms of Section 209 of the Act.
 
 
            Ministry's Comments (15.09.04):-
 
            Cost Accounting Records (Electricity Industry) Rules, 2001, by virtue of Sub- Rule 2 of Rule 1 have become
applicable w.e.f. 21st December, 2001. According to Sub- Rule (1) of Rule 3, every Company in the Electricity Industry to
which these rules apply, shall keep proper books of accounts u/s 209 (1) (d) of Companies Act, 1956 from the financial year
commencing on or after 21.12.2001.
 
 
           
2.)        Point Raised:-
 
            Rule 4- Penalty: "If a company contravenes the provisions of rule 3, the company and every officer thereof who is in
default, including the persons referred to in sub-rule (4) of rule 3 shall, subject to provisions of section 209 of Companies
Act, 1956 (1 of 1956), be punishable with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees and where the contravention is a
continuing one, with a further fine which may extend to five hundred rupees for every day, after the first day during which
such contravention continues."
 
            The rules have been framed in pursuance to section 209 of the Companies Act, 1956. Section 209 (5) prescribes for a
penalty of imprisonment up to 6 months and / or with fine up to Rs. 1000/- in case of failure to secure compliance of

provisions of section 209 by a company. The provisions of rule 4 are subject to the provisions of section 209 of the Act. On
what basis, Government are supplementing the penal provisions through subordinate legislation; should these appropriately
not form part of the principal Act?
 
            Ministry' Comments:-
 
            The Cost Accounting Records (Electricity Industry) Rules, 2001 have been framed in exercise of powers conferred by
section 642 (1) read with section 209 (1) (d) of the Companies Act, 1956. As per section 642 (2) of the said Act, "any rule
made under sub section (1) may provide that a contravention thereof shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five
thousand rupees and where the contravention is a continuing one, with a further fine which may extend to five hundred
rupees for every day, after the first day during which such contravention continues."
 
            As the empowering section for making these rules is section 642 (1) of the said Act, the penalty has been provided as
laid down under this section. Such penal provisions exist uniformly in all the rules prescribed under section 209 (1) (d) of
the said Act. Before notifying these rules, same were duly vetted by the Legislative Department also.
 
3.)        Point Raised:-
 
            A perusal of the provisions of the schedule as well as proformae A-F which have been appended to the rules give an
understanding that any company engaged in generation, transmission or bulk supply and distribution and retail supply of
electricity is required to keep a record of a large volume of information with very minute details. Further, the provisions of
the schedule, at a number of places prescribe for maintenance of "proper records"
 in many of the areas like materials,
salaries and allowances, service department expenses, utilities, workshop or repair and maintenance or tool rooms, fixed
assets and depreciation and other overhead expenses, etc.
 
            What is the objective sought to be achieved by prescribing various companies in electricity industry to keep such
detailed records in respect of their activities; secondly, the term "proper records" appearing at different places in the
schedule is also capable of varied interpretation. Whether the Ministry have any objection in substituting the term "proper
records" by some other specific expression?
 
           
 
Ministry's Comments:-
 
Authentic cost data base is not only essential for the industries to improve upon their performance and face
competitive environment, but also is extensively utilized by various Government agencies, revenue authorities, regulatory
bodies and other institutions for meeting their respective objectives. Likely benefits to the companies from such rules have
also been indicated under various para of the rules.
 
            The term "proper records" means records maintained as per normally accepted accounting principles and practices.
The Ministry has no objection in substituting the term "proper records" by some other specific expression.
           
4.)        Point Raised:-
 
            To what extend, the requirement of these rules are being complied with by the various companies falling within its
purview and what feedback, if any, has been received by the Government with regard to the practicability of the strict
compliance of the provisions of these rules?
 
            Ministry's Comments:-
 
            Feedback on compliance of the provisions of these rules would be available after some time as the industry is
required to keep cost records from the financial year commencing on or after 21st December, 2001 in terms of Rule 3 supra.
 
 
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Company Affairs have carried out and notified all the
amendments in Cost Accounting Records ( Electricity Industry) Rules , 2001as recommended by it.

1.         Point referred
 
The Customs House (Agents’ Licensing) Regulations, 2004 have been brought into effect in supersession of the
regulations of 1984.  What are the consideration that led Government to come out with a new set of regulations in
supersession of the earlier ones and what are the distinctive features of the new regulations?
Ministry's reply
A high powered “Committee on Transaction Cost of Indian Exports” headed by the then Secretary (Revenue) had
recommended in the year 1999, apart from other things, some changes in the CHA regulations to take into account the
changing role of Custom House Agents ( in relation to export activities).
Further, the Kelkar Committee on Indirect Taxes had also made recommendations in December, 2002, for
amendment to the CHALR, 1984, to make them more efficient and competent in promoting international trade.  This has
already been communicated to the field formations under Ministry’s letter F. No. 502/4/2004-CUS-VI dated 8
th March,
2004.
            The salient charges in CHLR, 2004 as compared to CHALR, 1984 are the following: -
1.
                  The system of giving temporary CHA licences has been abolished.
2.                  Written examination would be conducted by DGI on all India basis.
3.                  The CHAs will now be given a time period of seven years to pass both the written and oral examinations to be
eligible for a licence.
4.                  A CHA once licensed would be able to operate at all customs stations all over India after a simple intimation to
the jurisdictional Commissioner.
5.                  The fees to be charged by CHAs from their clients would be determined by market forces.
6.                  The period of validity of CHA licence would be ten years.
7.                  On the demise of the CHA, his legal heir would be allowed to continue with the CHA work subject to his
clearing the CHA examination within two years.
8.                  The educational qualification for CHA is being raised to that of a professional degree holder with working
knowledge of computers and customs procedures.  The CHA will also be required to be familiar with allied laws

3.      Point referred
 As per regulation 3, any person carrying on the business of a customs house agent should hold a licence granted
under the regulations.  But regulation 3 lays down three exceptions to this.  These exceptions are in the case of (i) an
importer or exporter transacting business solely on his own account, (ii) an employee of any person or a firm transacting
business generally on behalf of such person or firm and holding an I-card or temporary pass issued by the Deputy
Commissioner Customs and (iii) an agent employed for one or more vessels or aircrafts in order solely to enter or clear such
vessels or aircrafts for work incidental to such employment.
(i)
                 What is the basis and justification for granting exceptions as mentioned above?
(ii)The exceptions laid down as above do not seem to be specific, particularly, the words ‘generally’, ‘solely’ and
‘work incidental to’ tend to render the provisions for varied interpretations.  Whether Government have any objection
in reviewing the exceptions so as to make the provisions specific?

167th Report of Committee on Subordinate Legislation
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/167thReport.htm[25-10-2016 16:44:04]
Ministry's reply
            The licensing of CHAs is only to ensure that the importer/exporter gets the services of competent and efficient
professionals in expeditious clearance.   However, if any importer or exporter wishes to file his own documents and observe
all customs laws and procedures relating to import and export of his own consignment it may not be proper to compel such
importer or exporter to bear the cost of engaging a CHA.
            Similarly, a firm may assign one of its employees the exclusive job of clearing the firm’s consignments.  In this case
also it may not be appropriate to force the firm to engage the services of a CHA.
            In respect of vessels and aircrafts the clearance formalities in respect of regular voyages or flights are mere
technicalities since a vessel docking at a port is technically an import and a vessel leaving a port is technically an export. 
Same is the case with aircrafts.  The agent of the airlines or shipping lines is technically equipped to handle the customs
formalities, and so it would not be fair to compel such airlines/shipping lines to engage the services of CHAs.
            The word “generally” used in clause (ii) above is to cover a situation where the employee may be doing some other
work also in the firm apart from that relating to clearance of cargo.
            As regards use of the words “solely” and “work incidental to” they are meant to differentiate the clearance of
vessel/aircraft coming on regular voyage or trip from, say, regular import of a vessel for use within coastal waters or for
breaking-up.  In respect of aircrafts it would relate to regular import of an aircraft for domestic use in India.  In case of
commercial shipping it is the shipping agent who “solely” handles the import and export formalities and such work is only
“incidental to” his regular employment which is to get cargo booking.  Same is the case in respect of airlines.
            Since these expressions have been in use for more then 20 years  (it was there in the earlier Regulations also) without
any implementation problems no useful purpose will be served in reviewing/amending these provisions now.
Committee's Observations (25/10/2004)
The Committee had taken exception to the use of terms like “generally”, “solely” and “work incidental to” in
Regulation 3 while prescribing exceptions to the requirement of holding a license by a person to carry on the business of a
customs house agent.
            The Committee was informed that the provisions of Regulations 3 had not caused any inconvenience to the
department and, therefore, the existing provisions could be retained.
Committee's Observations (9/11/2005)
            The Committee pointed out that the Ministry had not carried out amendment in Regulation 3 and it desired to know
the views of the representatives at Bangalore on the Committee’s suggestion on Regulation 3.  The Committee noted that the
representatives Bangalore Commissionerate also did not feel the necessity of any change in Regulation 3.
4.
      Point referred
As per regulation 4, the Commissioner of Customs has been authorized to invite applications for grant of such
number of licences as assessed by him to act as customs house agents by means of notice as well as through publication in at
least two newspapers.  What is the basis of assessing the number of licences to be granted? Secondly, whether Government
are putting such notices on Department’s website also and, if so, would it    not be appropriate to provide for it in the
regulations?
Ministry's reply
            The Commissioner of Customs assesses the number of licenses to be granted on the basis of the workload in the
customs stations and the number of CHAs available to handle such work.  Though some guidelines have been framed (1000
documents per CHA per year for major Custom House and 500 documents per CHA per year for other ports) for assessing
requirement of additional CHAs these are more in the nature of guiding principles rather than statutory requirements.
(Instructions F. No. 502/5/93-Custom VI dated 18.5.1994).
            There are no instructions right now that every such notice should necessarily be placed on the Department’s website

th Report of the
Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha.
 
 
                    The Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993 and the rules framed thereunder were
examined by the Committee. The matter was reported to the House by the Committee on 12th June, 1998 vide its 118th
Report, and the same was forwarded to the Ministry of Finance, Banking Division, for action taken note. The action taken
note furnished by the Ministry was perused by the Committee and the matter was again reported to the House on 14
th March,
2000 vide 128th Report of the Committee. The Committee in its 128th Report had recommended as under: -
            "The Committee considered the subject matter at its meeting held on 1st march 2000. The Committee notes with
satisfaction that its recommendations vide paras 4.4 (b) (d) and (g) have found favour with the Ministry of Finance. The
Committee hopes that the legislation incorporating the Committee's suggestions will be got passed through Parliament by the
Ministry of Finance during the on- going Budget Session. As regards the Committee's recommendation as contained in para
4.4 (g), it notes with satisfaction the comments of Ministry of Finance that the suggestion, which requires amendment to the
rules, would be considered in the next stage. The Committee, in this context, recommends further that the new rules should
also empower the Tribunal to notify the defaulters names even on the website of the DRT/Bank/Financial Institution.
            The Committee thereafter took up for consideration the comments of the Ministry of Finance as also the
recommendations of the Working Group of the Reserve Bank of India with regard to paras 4.4 (a), (e) and (f) of the 118
th
report of the Committee. On the Committee's recommendation vide para 4.4 (a) for restructuring of Debt Recovery Tribunals
and Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunals on the lines of the Revenue Courts and Special Courts with codified rules, the
Committee notes the observation of the Working Group of the Reserve Bank of India in the matter viz. that no specific
advantage is foreseen by effecting such a change. The Committee decides not to pursue this recommendation further. The
Committee also agrees with the suggestion of the Working Group of the Reserve Bank of India on its recommendation as
contained in para 4.4(f) regarding authorization of the Tribunals under the Act/Rules to order deposit of 50% of the
certificate amount while setting aside an ex-party order. The Committee agrees that such issues should be better left at the
discretion of the Presiding Officer of the Debt Recovery Tribunal.
The Committee reviewed its recommendation as contained in para 4.4 (e) regarding lowering of the fiscal limit from

th Report were forwarded to the Ministry of Finance for necessary action on the

 1.        Recommendations of the Committee on para (4.4 (a))  (118th  Report )                            
               Debts Recovery Tribunals and Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunals should be restructured on the lines of Revenue
Courts/Special Courts with codified rules and procedure like code of civil procedure and be liberated from the deemed
judicial status to a full fledged judicial authority exclusively for the purpose of recovery of debts with adequate infrastructure
so as to make the systems meaningful, effective and deterrent.
Opinion of the Working Group
   As regards the suggestion made by the Committee in para 4.4 (a) of the Report, that the DRT and DRATs could be
restructured on the lines of Revenue Courts, Special Courts with codified rules and procedure and liberated from the deemed
judicial status. In the opinion of the working Group, there is no need to make any structural change in the status of the DRTs
or DRATs. While appreciating the suggestion made by the Committee, the Working Group does not find any specific
advantage in making change in the structure of the tribunals as the purpose for establishing the DRTs can be achieved with
same force without being subjected to the rigour of the codified procedure and law. In para 2.28 of the report, the Working
Group has already recommended the penal provision for non-compliance with the order by the tribunal. This will make
DRTs and DRATs more effective and deterrent.

Opinion of the Working Group
                In para 4.4 (e), the suggestion made by the Committee is that the Central Government may notify that the
provisions of the Act shall also apply to the cases of not less than Rs. 2 lakh and also widening the definition of "Debt" to
include the liability of any persons to the banks and financial institutions and should also specifically include any debt
secured by mortgage, hypothecation, pledge, etc. The Working Group is of the opinion that having regard to the
infrastructural constraints and large number of court cases, which have been transferred to the DRTs under Section 31 of the
Act, there is acute pressure on the DRTs, resulting in inordinate delay in disposal of applications pending before them. Once
recommendations made by the Working Group to appoint more DRTs is accepted by the Government and the number of
pending cases before them come down, the Government may consider lowering the present limit of Rs. 10 lakh in terms of
Section. 1(4) of the Act, so that more cases of recovery of bank dues are covered by the DRTs. As regards the suggestion to
widen in the definition of "debt", to include debts secured by mortgage, hypothecation, etc., the Working Group finds that
the expression "debt" as defined in Section 2 (g) of the Act, already includes dues from any person whether secured or
unsecured, subsisting and legally recoverable on the date of application. Since the secured debt is already included in the
definition of "debt", it is not necessary to specifically mention debts secured by mortgage, hypothecation, pledge or
otherwise in the definition of the "debt".

setting aside the ex-party order on flimsy grounds. There should be a provision in the Act/ Rules to the effect that if the
Tribunal is satisfied and decides to set aside the ex-party order, then that order would be subject to payment of 50% of the
certificate amount.
Opinion of the Working Group
               In para 4.4(f), the Committee has observed that the defendants are generally avoiding participation in the
proceedings before the tribunal, leading to ex-parte orders, but at the stage of certificate proceedings, they appear before the
tribunal and pray for the setting aside ex-parte orders on flimsy grounds. The Committee has, therefore, proposed that there
should be provision in the Act/Rules that if the tribunal is satisfied and decides to set aside ex-parte order, then the order
should be made subject to payment of 50% of the certificate amount. The Working Group in para 2.14 of the report, has
recommended that it should be the duty of the applicant bank/financial institution to ensure that the due service is effected on
the borrower. Once the lending banks/institutions take interest in effecting service of notices on their borrowers, the
borrower is unlikely to remain absent from the proceedings and in spite of the proper service on him, he chooses not to
participate in the proceedings and the ex-parte order is passed by the tribunal, the tribunals should avoid entertaining requests
for setting aside such ex-parte order is passed by the tribunal, the tribunals should avoid entertaining requests for setting
aside such ex-parte orders unless very cogent reasons are shown by the borrower/defendant why he could not participate in
the proceedings on the notified date. In such a case, in the opinion of the Working Group, it should be left to the discretion of
the PO of DRTs to decide whether to set aside such ex-parte order and if so, subject to what terms. However, it will not be
proper to curtail the discretion of the PO by providing payment of 50% of the certificate amount of setting aside such ex-
parte order.
            Action taken note (21/5/2001)                                                                              
   Keeping in view the opinion of the Working Group no action appears necessary in this issue.

defaulters after the decrees have been passed. In the opinion of the Working Group, the suggestion is welcomed and we
recommend accordingly. However, such notification of names of defaulters should be done only after the period prescribed

167th Report of Committee on Subordinate Legislation
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/167thReport.htm[25-10-2016 16:44:04]
        Ministry’s comments: (12.5 2004)
The corresponding provisions in earlier Regulations provided for a time limit of 30 days from the hearing date within
which the Chairman would have to pass orders.  In two cases, where the order could not be passed within the said limit, SAT
held that if the order is not passed within the stipulated time, then in such cases Chairman/Member becomes functus officio
and thereafter no order can be passed.  Therefore, the amendment has been made to provide for passing the order ‘as soon as
possible’ so that the intermediary shall not escape penalty on mere technicalities.  Though it is desirable, it is not always
possible to adhere to a rigid time limit within which the Chairman/Member should pass the order in view of the various
technicalities and peculiarities which may be present in a particular case.  Some cases require further inquiries/investigation
in view of the submissions of the party or may require appreciation of voluminous evidence.  Some may involve complicated
questions of law on which legal opinion may have to be taken.  In some other cases, the order is not being able to be passed
on account of litigation pending before Courts/Tribunals.  Therefore, it is felt that a rigid time limit which may lead to non-
compliant orders being treated as non est in law may seriously jeopardize regulatory efforts in such cases.
It is further felt that such time limits are not mentioned in any relevant regulatory statutes.  Even in respect of
adjudications by Adjudication Officers of SEBI, section 151(2) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with rule 5(1) of the SEBI
(Procedure for Holding Inquiry by Adjudication Officers and Imposing Penalty) Rules, 1995 do not specify any time limit
within which the Adjudication Officer should pass the order imposing monetary penalty.  Even in respect of original
regulatory adjudications under other statutes, no provisions are found wherein time limits have been stipulated for passing of
orders.  An example is section 13 of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 read with rule 4(8) of the Foreign
Exchange Management (Adjudicating and Appeals) Rules, 2000 which merely say that the Adjudicating Authority can by
order, impose appropriate penalty.  Similar were the provisions under section 50 of the erstwhile Foreign Exchange
Regulation Act, 1973 read with rule 3 of the Adjudication Proceedings and Appeal Rules, 1974.  Section 11AC of the
Central Excise Act, 1944 read with rules 25 to 27 of the Central Excise Rules, 2002 and section 122 of the Customs Act,
1962 also do not contain any time limit for passing an order of imposition of penalty or confiscation of goods.
     Committee’s observation :(7.2.2005)
The Committee noted that SEBI had accepted its suggestion to find out a via-media and amended the regulations
appropriately with regarding prescription of time limit for passing order by the Chairman/ Member.
     Action Taken by the Ministry (7.6.2005)
The Ministry have notified the amendment as suggested by the Committee.

Government by adding the words "the following regulations as amended from time to time".
            · Regulation 16( 3)(i) & (2) :
 The word 'ordinarily' has been substituted by the words 'Provided that the Enquiry
Officer may extend the time mentioned under sub-legislation (2 ) for sufficient reasons to be recorded in writing', thereby
removing ambiguity in the provision regarding extension of time during the enquiry.
            The Committee, however, notes with satisfaction the explanation furnished by the Ministry with regard to Regulation
5 (1) (point no 1), regulations 7 and 22 (point no 2), and regulation 13 (point no 4).
VI
 
The Committee notes with satisfaction that based upon the its recommendation the Ministry of Environment & Forests
have amended Rules 4 by adding a new sub rule (3) which places an obligation upon the SPCBs and PCCs to collect, compile and
publish technical and statistical data in consultation with the CPCB relating to noise pollution and measure devised for its effective
prevention, control and abatement. The Committee feels that this would result in better and effective implementation of the rules.
            The Committee further notes with satisfaction that Government have amended rules 8 as well thereby providing an
opportunity to the complainant also to be heard while the Authority regulating noise levels reviews its orders based inter- alia on a
complaint, as suggested by it.
